name: Saccharine Trust
label: SST
lede: Jack Brewer preached from the mic and Joe Baiza, who still doesn't think of himself as a guitar player, ran jazz through punk a floor above D. Boon. SST treated them as the label's odd one out, and Kurt Cobain put Paganicons in his top 50.

eras.title: Downstairs from D. Boon
eras.text: Brewer and Baiza met in Wilmington looking for summer jobs and built a band out of Brewer's new wave group. Baiza lived downstairs from the Minutemen's D. Boon, and the two bands grew up side by side.

years.h: Jack Brewer's new wave band the Obstacles becomes Saccharine Trust
years.p: [[Joe Baiza|4dfac6b9-47a7-4521-9a3d-32b0740e61d3]] joins on bass and steers it toward punk. When the others drift away, he and Brewer keep going and take the name from David Bowie's The Bewlay Brothers.
years.xp:
The lineup took almost a year to settle. According to Wikipedia, one of the people who auditioned and didn't get the job was [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]].

Baiza lived downstairs from [[D. Boon|ae1757eb-8679-4cb3-8d3a-33160c953505]] and heard the [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]] working out their sound before they had a name. Boon came down and introduced himself after hearing Saccharine Trust practice.

Baiza told Vice he came at music as a beginner: "I approached music as a conceptual art project for myself."

years.h: Opening for the Minutemen, a first show Baiza dates to '79
years.p: The Minutemen were about six months old. The first lineup: Jack Brewer, Joe Baiza on guitar, Luis Maldonado on bass and Richie Wilder on drums.
years.xp: Baiza puts the show in 1979; Wikipedia says 1980. Wilder soon left for Mood of Defiance and Rob Holzman took over the drums. Maldonado wanted straight hardcore, not the jazz the band was drifting toward, and Earl Liberty replaced him.

years.h: Mike Watt's New Alliance comp puts them on tape first
years.p: Saccharine Trust record at [[Spot|d95a08a1-80f5-4232-bdb7-4777c369f0f9]]'s studio in Hermosa Beach for Watt's compilation of San Pedro bands, Cracks in the Sidewalk, on New Alliance Records.
years.xp: Baiza drew artwork for the comp, and Watt turned it down. Baiza used it on Paganicons instead.

years.cap: Flyer for a Cuckoo's Nest show in Costa Mesa: Minutemen, Descendents, Saccharine Trust and Overkill, 1981
years.h: Greg Ginn and Chuck Dukowski walk up after a Star Theater set
years.p: [[Black Flag|9941a936-196a-4a62-ae53-a69cbc33f20e]] had invited Saccharine Trust to open at the Star Theater in San Pedro. Afterwards [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]] and [[Chuck Dukowski|19a07153-933f-4725-a5de-477cb3554517]] asked them to record for SST.
years.xp: Baiza remembers the moment in Vice: "Greg Ginn and Chuck Dukowski came by after and surprised us by asking to record on SST."

years.h: Paganicons becomes SST 006
years.p: Recorded in April 1981 at Media Art in Hermosa Beach with Spot and Mike Watt. Eight songs, from the 36-second Mad at the Co. to the five-minute A Human Certainty.
years.xp:
The lineup was Jack Brewer, Joe Baiza, Earl Liberty and Rob Holzman, who then left for Slovenly. Brewer is credited as Joaquin Milhouse Brewer.

AllMusic's John Dougan found Brewer pretentious but singled out Baiza's abrasive guitar.

eras.title: Sermons, free jazz and Mike Watt on bass
eras.text: With Tony Cicero on drums and Baiza deep into jazz, the band stopped sounding like anything else on SST. Brewer credited himself with sermons, a whole live album was made up on the spot, and Watt produced the last record.

years.h: Tony Cicero and Mark Hodson join Brewer and Baiza at Total Access
years.p: The four record Surviving You, Always in Redondo Beach in September, with Spot at the board.

years.h: On Surviving You, Always, Brewer's credit reads vocals and sermons
years.p: Biblical imagery, a cornet on Yhwh on Acid and a cover of the Doors' Peace Frog. The cover uses Robert Wiles' photo of Evelyn McHale, who jumped from the Empire State Building in 1947.
years.xp:
Wikipedia notes Brewer's interest in the TV minister Gene Scott. Baiza was exploring jazz, and it shows.

Trouser Press heard a band using the punk idiom like avant-jazz, with Brewer's vocals as blurt poetry over structured riffs. AllMusic's John Dougan, on the earlier Paganicons, found Brewer pretentious but singled out Baiza's abrasive guitar.

years.h: God Bows to Math carries Jack Brewer's words on a Minutemen record
years.p: Brewer writes the lyrics to God Bows to Math on the Minutemen's Double Nickels on the Dime. The two bands were constant SST billmates.

years.big: four tuxedoed gents bravely fighting the incessant urge-to-riff
years.h: At McCabe's in Santa Monica, a whole set is made up on the spot
years.p: That's Byron Coley on the band. Behind Jack Brewer's poems, Joe Baiza and Mike Watt, on bass after Mark Hodson's exit, improvise the entire set, and SST releases the tape as Worldbroken.
years.xp:
SST's [[Joe Carducci|6f08ef70-2da6-4575-8ec2-22438145f5d2]] suggested bringing in Watt, and drew the cover. Tony Cicero later called it "amazing and challenging in many ways, recorded live with an audience."

It later shaped the Unknown Instructors, and bassist Damon Smith said it changed how he heard punk, jazz and free playing.

years.h: A saxophone and a fifth member arrive for We Became Snakes
years.p: [[Mike Watt|568203ae-c27b-4990-8997-09c0d5c0de77]] produces. Saccharine Trust grow to a five-piece with a new bassist, and it's their last studio album for fifteen years.
years.xp: Trouser Press called it "imaginative and far-reaching, if not exactly enjoyable or accessible."

yt: Live at d.c. space, Washington, 1986 (partial set)
years.h: Saccharine Trust stop, and Baiza heads for Universal Congress Of
years.p: Around 1986 the band is done. SST puts out the compilation The Sacramental Element the same year, and Joe Baiza moves on to the jazz-punk band [[Universal Congress Of|d0478192-4d5a-4180-a627-da061ba22a66]].

eras.title: The tapes keep going, the band doesn't
eras.text: While the band was gone, SST kept the name alive with a live archive and Sonic Youth covered its best-known song. In the mid-1990s Brewer and Baiza came back with a rhythm section Baiza says has been together longer than the original one.

years.h: Sonic Youth pick I Am Right off Paganicons
years.p: [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] record it for SST's compilation The Melting Plot.

years.h: Past Lives pulls 75 minutes from seven years of live tapes
years.p: From shamanic jams to quiet improvisation, recorded well and badly across the band's whole run.

years.h: Brewer starts his own band, then writes a book
years.p: The Jack Brewer Band releases Rockin' Ethereal on New Alliance. He later records with the jazz trio Bazooka and publishes Rhythm or Suicide, a book of poems and writings.

years.h: After a decade, Brewer and Baiza call in a new rhythm section
years.p: Drummer Brian Christopherson and, by 1997, bassist Chris Stein join Jack Brewer and Joe Baiza. They play up and down the West Coast.
years.xp: Baiza told Vice the Christopherson and Stein lineup "has been together longer than the original one." Wikipedia has him calling it the best version of the band.

years.h: The Great One Is Dead ends a 15-year gap
years.p: The reunited lineup's album comes out on Hazelwood. Recess Records reissues it as a double LP in 2017.

eras.title: Cobain's list, Ginn's vault
eras.text: Kurt Cobain's journals and a later wave of free-jazz punks gave the band a reputation it never had at the time. The early records stayed with SST.

years.h: Kurt Cobain lists Paganicons among his favorite records
years.p: [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]]'s published Journals include it in his top 50. OC Weekly places it ninth.

years.h: Brewer and Baiza join two Minutemen as the Unknown Instructors
years.p: With Mike Watt and [[George Hurley|e3644b83-1c19-41fa-bf81-483551cd1588]] they make The Way Things Work, a project built on the Worldbroken idea.

q: Greg Ginn at SST still won't allow anything to be done with it.
years.h: Baiza says Greg Ginn is still sitting on the catalog
years.p: Joe Baiza tells Vice that SST's Greg Ginn won't allow anything to be done with the band's records, and calls Saccharine Trust the black sheep of the roster.
years.xp: In the same interview Baiza says the Minutemen taught him that in a band you have to really put out, and that he still doesn't think of himself as a guitar player.

years.h: Bassist Chris Stein dies at 44
years.p: OC Weekly reported he died December 1 after a two-year cancer fight that spread to his brain. He'd been in the band since 1997.
years.xp:
Stein also played in Citizen Down with Jason Cruz before [[Strung Out|0220a594-56a1-47ca-8288-001ead3a3546]], and later in Jason Cruz and Howl. He reworked the bass lines in I Am Right in a way that impressed even the band's original bassist.

His own rule, he told Cruz: "The song is the boss."

sources.title: Vice: Talking About Minutemen and SST with Joe Baiza
Todestrieb: 35 Years Ago, Saccharine Trust record Worldbroken
